```{r combined_any_2024_vs_2020_tests}
# ── 2024 vs 2020 Comparisons for Combined Exposure (Nature reporting) ───────
# Each metric: weighted t-test, Cohen's d, 95% CIs

# 1. % Exposed comparison
combined_exp_test <- weights::wtd.t.test(
  x = main_2024$combined_any_flag, weight = main_2024$weight,
  y = main_2020$combined_any_flag, weighty = main_2020$weight
)
sd_exp_2024 <- sqrt(Hmisc::wtd.var(x = main_2024$combined_any_flag, weights = main_2024$weight))
sd_exp_2020 <- sqrt(Hmisc::wtd.var(x = main_2020$combined_any_flag, weights = main_2020$weight))
pooled_sd_exp <- sqrt((sd_exp_2024^2 + sd_exp_2020^2) / 2)
cohens_d_exp <- (combined_exp_test$additional[["Mean.x"]] - combined_exp_test$additional[["Mean.y"]]) / pooled_sd_exp

# Difference CI
diff_exp <- combined_exposure_2024$mean - combined_exposure_2020$mean
diff_se_exp <- sqrt(combined_exposure_2024$se^2 + combined_exposure_2020$se^2)

# 2. Intensity among exposed comparison
combined_int_test <- weights::wtd.t.test(
  x = exposed_combined_2024$combined_any_n, weight = exposed_combined_2024$weight,
  y = exposed_combined_2020$combined_any_n, weighty = exposed_combined_2020$weight
)
sd_int_2024 <- sqrt(Hmisc::wtd.var(x = exposed_combined_2024$combined_any_n, weights = exposed_combined_2024$weight))
sd_int_2020 <- sqrt(Hmisc::wtd.var(x = exposed_combined_2020$combined_any_n, weights = exposed_combined_2020$weight))
pooled_sd_int <- sqrt((sd_int_2024^2 + sd_int_2020^2) / 2)
cohens_d_int <- (combined_int_test$additional[["Mean.x"]] - combined_int_test$additional[["Mean.y"]]) / pooled_sd_int

# Difference CI
diff_int <- combined_intensity_2024$mean - combined_intensity_2020$mean
diff_se_int <- sqrt(combined_intensity_2024$se^2 + combined_intensity_2020$se^2)

# 3. % of all visits comparison
combined_pct_all_test <- weights::wtd.t.test(
  x = main_2024$percentage_visits_combined_any, weight = main_2024$weight,
  y = main_2020$percentage_visits_combined_any, weighty = main_2020$weight
)
sd_pct_all_2024 <- sqrt(Hmisc::wtd.var(x = main_2024$percentage_visits_combined_any, weights = main_2024$weight))
sd_pct_all_2020 <- sqrt(Hmisc::wtd.var(x = main_2020$percentage_visits_combined_any, weights = main_2020$weight))
pooled_sd_pct_all <- sqrt((sd_pct_all_2024^2 + sd_pct_all_2020^2) / 2)
cohens_d_pct_all <- (combined_pct_all_test$additional[["Mean.x"]] - combined_pct_all_test$additional[["Mean.y"]]) / pooled_sd_pct_all

# Difference CI
diff_pct_all <- combined_pct_all_2024$mean - combined_pct_all_2020$mean
diff_se_pct_all <- sqrt(combined_pct_all_2024$se^2 + combined_pct_all_2020$se^2)

# 4. % of news visits comparison
combined_pct_news_test <- weights::wtd.t.test(
  x = main_2024$pct_news_combined_any, weight = main_2024$weight,
  y = main_2020$pct_news_combined_any, weighty = main_2020$weight
)
sd_pct_news_2024 <- sqrt(Hmisc::wtd.var(x = main_2024$pct_news_combined_any, weights = main_2024$weight))
sd_pct_news_2020 <- sqrt(Hmisc::wtd.var(x = main_2020$pct_news_combined_any, weights = main_2020$weight))
pooled_sd_pct_news <- sqrt((sd_pct_news_2024^2 + sd_pct_news_2020^2) / 2)
cohens_d_pct_news <- (combined_pct_news_test$additional[["Mean.x"]] - combined_pct_news_test$additional[["Mean.y"]]) / pooled_sd_pct_news

# Difference CI
diff_pct_news <- combined_pct_news_2024$mean - combined_pct_news_2020$mean
diff_se_pct_news <- sqrt(combined_pct_news_2024$se^2 + combined_pct_news_2020$se^2)

# --- Full comparison table ---
combined_comparison_table <- tibble::tibble(
  Metric = c("% Exposed", "Mean Visits (Among Exposed)", "% of All Visits", "% of News Visits"),
  `2024 [95% CI]` = c(
    paste0(scales::percent(combined_exposure_2024$mean, accuracy = 0.1),
           " [", scales::percent(combined_exposure_2024$low, accuracy = 0.1), ", ",
           scales::percent(combined_exposure_2024$high, accuracy = 0.1), "]"),
    paste0(round(combined_intensity_2024$mean, 1),
           " [", round(combined_intensity_2024$low, 1), ", ",
           round(combined_intensity_2024$high, 1), "]"),
    paste0(sprintf("%.3f%%", combined_pct_all_2024$mean * 100),
           " [", sprintf("%.3f%%", combined_pct_all_2024$low * 100), ", ",
           sprintf("%.3f%%", combined_pct_all_2024$high * 100), "]"),
    paste0(sprintf("%.2f%%", combined_pct_news_2024$mean * 100),
           " [", sprintf("%.2f%%", combined_pct_news_2024$low * 100), ", ",
           sprintf("%.2f%%", combined_pct_news_2024$high * 100), "]")
  ),
  `2020 [95% CI]` = c(
    paste0(scales::percent(combined_exposure_2020$mean, accuracy = 0.1),
           " [", scales::percent(combined_exposure_2020$low, accuracy = 0.1), ", ",
           scales::percent(combined_exposure_2020$high, accuracy = 0.1), "]"),
    paste0(round(combined_intensity_2020$mean, 1),
           " [", round(combined_intensity_2020$low, 1), ", ",
           round(combined_intensity_2020$high, 1), "]"),
    paste0(sprintf("%.3f%%", combined_pct_all_2020$mean * 100),
           " [", sprintf("%.3f%%", combined_pct_all_2020$low * 100), ", ",
           sprintf("%.3f%%", combined_pct_all_2020$high * 100), "]"),
    paste0(sprintf("%.2f%%", combined_pct_news_2020$mean * 100),
           " [", sprintf("%.2f%%", combined_pct_news_2020$low * 100), ", ",
           sprintf("%.2f%%", combined_pct_news_2020$high * 100), "]")
  ),
  `Diff [95% CI]` = c(
    paste0(sprintf("%.1f%%", diff_exp * 100),
           " [", sprintf("%.1f%%", (diff_exp - 1.96 * diff_se_exp) * 100), ", ",
           sprintf("%.1f%%", (diff_exp + 1.96 * diff_se_exp) * 100), "]"),
    paste0(round(diff_int, 1),
           " [", round(diff_int - 1.96 * diff_se_int, 1), ", ",
           round(diff_int + 1.96 * diff_se_int, 1), "]"),
    paste0(sprintf("%.3f%%", diff_pct_all * 100),
           " [", sprintf("%.3f%%", (diff_pct_all - 1.96 * diff_se_pct_all) * 100), ", ",
           sprintf("%.3f%%", (diff_pct_all + 1.96 * diff_se_pct_all) * 100), "]"),
    paste0(sprintf("%.2f%%", diff_pct_news * 100),
           " [", sprintf("%.2f%%", (diff_pct_news - 1.96 * diff_se_pct_news) * 100), ", ",
           sprintf("%.2f%%", (diff_pct_news + 1.96 * diff_se_pct_news) * 100), "]")
  ),
  `n (2024)` = c(nrow(main_2024), nrow(exposed_combined_2024), nrow(main_2024), nrow(main_2024)),
  `n (2020)` = c(nrow(main_2020), nrow(exposed_combined_2020), nrow(main_2020), nrow(main_2020)),
  `t(df)` = c(
    sprintf("t(%.0f) = %.2f", combined_exp_test$coefficients["df"], combined_exp_test$coefficients["t.value"]),
    sprintf("t(%.0f) = %.2f", combined_int_test$coefficients["df"], combined_int_test$coefficients["t.value"]),
    sprintf("t(%.0f) = %.2f", combined_pct_all_test$coefficients["df"], combined_pct_all_test$coefficients["t.value"]),
    sprintf("t(%.0f) = %.2f", combined_pct_news_test$coefficients["df"], combined_pct_news_test$coefficients["t.value"])
  ),
  p = c(
    ifelse(combined_exp_test$coefficients["p.value"] < 0.001, "< 0.001",
           sprintf("%.3f", combined_exp_test$coefficients["p.value"])),
    ifelse(combined_int_test$coefficients["p.value"] < 0.001, "< 0.001",
           sprintf("%.3f", combined_int_test$coefficients["p.value"])),
    ifelse(combined_pct_all_test$coefficients["p.value"] < 0.001, "< 0.001",
           sprintf("%.3f", combined_pct_all_test$coefficients["p.value"])),
    ifelse(combined_pct_news_test$coefficients["p.value"] < 0.001, "< 0.001",
           sprintf("%.3f", combined_pct_news_test$coefficients["p.value"]))
  ),
  `Cohen's d` = c(
    round(cohens_d_exp, 3),
    round(cohens_d_int, 3),
    round(cohens_d_pct_all, 3),
    round(cohens_d_pct_news, 3)
  )
)

knitr::kable(combined_comparison_table,
             caption = "S26: Combined (General + AI) Untrustworthy Exposure — 2024 vs. 2020 Comparison",
             format = "markdown")
```


# 5. Omnibus Regression Models

```{r format_nhb_style_function}
# Function to format regression results in NHB paper style
format_nhb_style <- function(model, alpha = 0.05) {
  coef_table <- summary(model)$coefficients
  ci <- confint(model, level = 1 - alpha)
  
  formatted_results <- data.frame(
    term = rownames(coef_table),
    estimate = coef_table[, "Estimate"],
    std_error = coef_table[, "Std. Error"],
    p_value = coef_table[, "Pr(>|t|)"],
    ci_low = ci[,1],
    ci_high = ci[,2]
  ) %>%
    mutate(
      # Format beta with exactly 3 decimal places
      beta = sprintf("β=%.3f", estimate),
      # Format standard error with exactly 3 decimal places
      se = sprintf("s.e. %.3f", std_error),
      # Format p-values
      p_text = case_when(
        p_value < 0.001 ~ "P<0.001",
        TRUE ~ sprintf("P=%.3f", p_value)
      ),
      # Format confidence intervals with exactly 3 decimal places
      ci = sprintf("95%% CI %.3f to %.3f", ci_low, ci_high)
    ) %>%
    select(term, beta, se, p_text, ci)
  
  return(formatted_results)
}

# Function to create the final NHB style table
create_nhb_table <- function(model_2020, model_2024) {
  # Format results for both years
  results_2020 <- format_nhb_style(model_2020)
  results_2024 <- format_nhb_style(model_2024)
  
  # Create the combined table with side-by-side columns
  table_combined <- data.frame(
    Variable = results_2020$term,
    `2020` = paste(
      results_2020$beta, "\n",
      results_2020$se, "\n",
      results_2020$p_text, "\n",
      results_2020$ci
    ),
    `2024` = paste(
      results_2024$beta, "\n",
      results_2024$se, "\n",
      results_2024$p_text, "\n",
      results_2024$ci
    )
  )
  
  # Add R² and N
  table_combined <- rbind(
    table_combined,
    data.frame(
      Variable = "R²",
      `2020` = sprintf("%.3f", summary(model_2020)$r.squared),
      `2024` = sprintf("%.3f", summary(model_2024)$r.squared)
    ),
    data.frame(
      Variable = "N",
      `2020` = nrow(model_2020$model),
      `2024` = nrow(model_2024$model)
    )
  )
  
  return(table_combined)
}
```

```{r untrustworthy_models, results='asis'}
# Function to format a coefficient nicely - updated for three models
format_coef <- function(var_name, var_2016, var_2020, var_2024, is_shaded = FALSE) {
  est_2016 <- coef_2016[var_2016, "Estimate"]
  se_2016 <- coef_2016[var_2016, "Std. Error"]
  p_2016 <- coef_2016[var_2016, "Pr(>|t|)"]
  ci_low_2016 <- ci_2016[var_2016, 1]
  ci_high_2016 <- ci_2016[var_2016, 2]
  
  est_2020 <- coef_2020[var_2020, "Estimate"]
  se_2020 <- coef_2020[var_2020, "Std. Error"]
  p_2020 <- coef_2020[var_2020, "Pr(>|t|)"]
  ci_low_2020 <- ci_2020[var_2020, 1]
  ci_high_2020 <- ci_2020[var_2020, 2]
  
  est_2024 <- coef_2024[var_2024, "Estimate"]
  se_2024 <- coef_2024[var_2024, "Std. Error"]
  p_2024 <- coef_2024[var_2024, "Pr(>|t|)"]
  ci_low_2024 <- ci_2024[var_2024, 1]
  ci_high_2024 <- ci_2024[var_2024, 2]
  
  p_text_2016 <- ifelse(p_2016 < 0.001, "P<0.001", paste0("P=", sprintf("%.3f", p_2016)))
  p_text_2020 <- ifelse(p_2020 < 0.001, "P<0.001", paste0("P=", sprintf("%.3f", p_2020)))
  p_text_2024 <- ifelse(p_2024 < 0.001, "P<0.001", paste0("P=", sprintf("%.3f", p_2024)))
  
  # Add shading for the entire variable group if requested
  if (is_shaded) {
    cat("\\rowcolor[gray]{0.93}\n")
  }
  
  # Print variable name row
  cat(sprintf("%s & $\\beta=%.3f$ & $\\beta=%.3f$ & $\\beta=%.3f$ \\\\ \n", 
              var_name, est_2016, est_2020, est_2024))
  
  # Continue with the same shading for all rows in this variable group
  if (is_shaded) {
    cat("\\rowcolor[gray]{0.93}\n")
  }
  cat(sprintf(" & s.e. %.3f & s.e. %.3f & s.e. %.3f \\\\ \n", 
              se_2016, se_2020, se_2024))
  
  if (is_shaded) {
    cat("\\rowcolor[gray]{0.93}\n")
  }
  cat(sprintf(" & %s & %s & %s \\\\ \n", 
              p_text_2016, p_text_2020, p_text_2024))
  
  if (is_shaded) {
    cat("\\rowcolor[gray]{0.93}\n")
  }
  cat(sprintf(" & 95\\%% CI %.3f to %.3f & 95\\%% CI %.3f to %.3f & 95\\%% CI %.3f to %.3f \\\\ \n", 
              ci_low_2016, ci_high_2016, ci_low_2020, ci_high_2020, ci_low_2024, ci_high_2024))
}

# Add variables with alternating shading
```

## 5.5 Multiple Testing Correction

This section applies multiple testing correction to the pre-registered hypotheses to control for family-wise error rate when testing multiple related hypotheses.

```{r multiple-testing-correction}
# Extract p-values from pre-registered hypothesis tests
# Note: p-values extracted from original test results in this script

# Pre-registered hypothesis p-values (saved from earlier analyses)
hypothesis_pvalues <- c(
  H1a = h1a_p,   # (one-sided: 2024 > 2020)
  H1b = h1b_p,   # (one-sided: 2024 < 2020)
  H2a = h2a_p,   # (one-sided: 2024 > 2020 intensity)
  H2b = h2b_p,   # (one-sided: 2024 < 2020 intensity)
  # H3a = h3a_p,   # (one-sided: 2024 > 2020 duration)
  # H3b = h3b_p,   # (one-sided: 2024 < 2020 duration)
  H4 = h4_p,     # Age regression p-value
  H5 = h5_p,     # Republican regression p-value
  # H6 = h6_p,     # Twitter referral chi-square test p-value
  H7 = h7_p,     # AI exposure increase test
  H8 = h8_p,     # AI proportion test p-value (one-sided)
  # H9 = h9_p,     # AI vs non-AI duration test
  H10 = h10_p,   # Age AI regression p-value
  H11 = h11_p    # Republican AI regression p-value
)

# Apply multiple testing corrections
# n = 14: total pre-registered hypotheses (H1a/b, H2a/b, H3a/b, H4-H11)
holm_adjusted <- p.adjust(hypothesis_pvalues, n = 14, method = "holm")
bonferroni_adjusted <- p.adjust(hypothesis_pvalues, n = 14, method = "bonferroni")

# Create results table
multiple_testing_results <- data.frame(
  hypothesis = names(hypothesis_pvalues),
  description = c(
    "2024 > 2020 exposure",
    "2024 < 2020 exposure",
    "2024 > 2020 intensity",
    "2024 < 2020 intensity",
    # "2024 > 2020 duration",
    # "2024 < 2020 duration",
    "Age 65+ > 18-29 exposure",
    "Republicans > Democrats exposure",
    # "Twitter refs 2024 > 2020",
    "AI exposure 2024 > 2020",
    "AI proportion 2024 > 2020",
    # "AI > non-AI duration",
    "Age 65+ > 18-29 AI exposure",
    "Republicans > Democrats AI exposure"
  ),
  original_p = hypothesis_pvalues,
  holm_adjusted_p = holm_adjusted,
  bonferroni_adjusted_p = bonferroni_adjusted,
  holm_significant = ifelse(holm_adjusted < 0.05, "Yes", "No"),
  bonferroni_significant = ifelse(bonferroni_adjusted < 0.05, "Yes", "No")
)

# Format p-values for display
multiple_testing_results$original_p_formatted <- ifelse(
  multiple_testing_results$original_p < 0.001,
  "< 0.001",
  sprintf("%.3f", multiple_testing_results$original_p)
)

multiple_testing_results$holm_adjusted_p_formatted <- ifelse(
  multiple_testing_results$holm_adjusted_p < 0.001,
  "< 0.001",
  sprintf("%.3f", multiple_testing_results$holm_adjusted_p)
)

multiple_testing_results$bonferroni_adjusted_p_formatted <- ifelse(
  multiple_testing_results$bonferroni_adjusted_p < 0.001,
  "< 0.001",
  sprintf("%.3f", multiple_testing_results$bonferroni_adjusted_p)
)

# Print summary
cat("Multiple Testing Correction Summary:\n")
cat("Total pre-registered hypotheses: 14\n")
cat("Originally significant (p < 0.05):", sum(hypothesis_pvalues < 0.05), "\n")
cat("Significant after Holm correction:", sum(holm_adjusted < 0.05), "\n")
cat("Significant after Bonferroni correction:", sum(bonferroni_adjusted < 0.05), "\n\n")
```

```{r multiple-testing-table}
# Create formatted table for output
kable(
  multiple_testing_results[, c("hypothesis", "description", "original_p_formatted",
                               "holm_adjusted_p_formatted", "bonferroni_adjusted_p_formatted",
                               "holm_significant", "bonferroni_significant")],
  col.names = c("Hypothesis", "Description", "Original P", "Holm P", "Bonferroni P",
                "Holm Sig.", "Bonf. Sig."),
  caption = "Multiple Testing Correction for Pre-Registered Hypotheses",
  align = c("l", "l", "r", "r", "r", "c", "c")
) %>%
  kable_styling(latex_options = c("scale_down", "hold_position"))
```

**Statistical Note:** Multiple testing correction was applied to the `r length(hypothesis_pvalues)` pre-registered hypotheses to control the family-wise error rate. The Holm-Bonferroni method provides a less conservative adjustment than the standard Bonferroni correction while still maintaining strong control over Type I error. For hypotheses H4, H5, H10, and H11, regression p-values from the omnibus models were used as these represent the pre-registered analytical approach that controls for potential confounding variables.

## 5.6 Ideological Composition of Untrustworthy Domains

SUPPLY-SIDE COMPOSITION REQUIRES NEWSGUARD'S PROPRIETARY DOMAIN RATINGS, WHICH WE ARE CONTRACTUALLY PROHIBITED FROM REDISTRIBUTING.

```{r ideology_composition_demand}
# ============================================================
# DEMAND: Topline metrics by domain ideology (from person-level CSV)
# ============================================================

# Verification: ideology-specific counts sum to total
stopifnot(all(main_2024$right_untrustworthy_n + main_2024$left_untrustworthy_n +
              main_2024$unclassified_untrustworthy_n == main_2024$untrustworthy_n))

cat("=== DEMAND: Topline Metrics by Domain Ideology ===\n\n")

# % Exposed
for (ideo in c("right", "left")) {
  flag_col <- paste0(ideo, "_untrustworthy_flag")
  m <- diagis::weighted_mean(x = main_2024[[flag_col]], w = main_2024$weight) * 100
  se <- diagis::weighted_se(x = main_2024[[flag_col]], w = main_2024$weight) * 100
  cat(sprintf("%s-leaning: %.1f%% exposed (95%% CI [%.1f%%, %.1f%%])\n",
              tools::toTitleCase(ideo), m, m - 1.96*se, m + 1.96*se))
}

# Visits among exposed
cat("\nVisits among exposed:\n")
for (ideo in c("right", "left")) {
  flag_col <- paste0(ideo, "_untrustworthy_flag")
  n_col <- paste0(ideo, "_untrustworthy_n")
  exposed <- main_2024 %>% filter(!!sym(flag_col) == 1)
  m <- diagis::weighted_mean(x = exposed[[n_col]], w = exposed$weight)
  se <- diagis::weighted_se(x = exposed[[n_col]], w = exposed$weight)
  cat(sprintf("  %s-leaning: %.1f visits (95%% CI [%.1f, %.1f]), n=%d\n",
              tools::toTitleCase(ideo), m, m - 1.96*se, m + 1.96*se, nrow(exposed)))
}

# % of total web visits
cat("\n% of total web visits:\n")
for (ideo in c("right", "left")) {
  col <- paste0("percentage_visits_", ideo, "_untrustworthy")
  m <- diagis::weighted_mean(x = main_2024[[col]], w = main_2024$weight) * 100
  se <- diagis::weighted_se(x = main_2024[[col]], w = main_2024$weight) * 100
  cat(sprintf("  %s-leaning: %.4f%% (95%% CI [%.4f%%, %.4f%%])\n",
              tools::toTitleCase(ideo), m, m - 1.96*se, m + 1.96*se))
}

# % of news visits
cat("\n% of news visits:\n")
for (ideo in c("right", "left")) {
  col <- paste0("pct_news_", ideo, "_untrustworthy")
  m <- diagis::weighted_mean(x = main_2024[[col]], w = main_2024$weight) * 100
  se <- diagis::weighted_se(x = main_2024[[col]], w = main_2024$weight) * 100
  cat(sprintf("  %s-leaning: %.2f%% (95%% CI [%.2f%%, %.2f%%])\n",
              tools::toTitleCase(ideo), m, m - 1.96*se, m + 1.96*se))
}

# Verification: decomposed metrics sum to originals
v_pct_total <- diagis::weighted_mean(
  x = main_2024$percentage_visits_right_untrustworthy +
      main_2024$percentage_visits_left_untrustworthy +
      ifelse(main_2024$total_visits > 0,
             main_2024$unclassified_untrustworthy_n / main_2024$total_visits, 0),
  w = main_2024$weight)
v_pct_total_orig <- diagis::weighted_mean(
  x = main_2024$percentage_visits_untrustworthy, w = main_2024$weight)
cat(sprintf("\nVerification (pct_total): sum=%.6f vs original=%.6f (match: %s)\n",
    v_pct_total, v_pct_total_orig, abs(v_pct_total - v_pct_total_orig) < 1e-10))

# Supply vs demand share (among classified visits)
total_right <- sum(main_2024$right_untrustworthy_n)
total_left <- sum(main_2024$left_untrustworthy_n)
demand_right_pct <- 100 * total_right / (total_right + total_left)
demand_left_pct <- 100 * total_left / (total_right + total_left)
cat(sprintf("\nDemand (classified visits): Right = %d (%.1f%%), Left = %d (%.1f%%)\n",
    total_right, demand_right_pct, total_left, demand_left_pct))
```

```{r ideology_partisan_moderated}
# ============================================================
# PARTISAN-MODERATED: Exposure by party × domain ideology
# ============================================================

rep_data <- main_2024 %>% filter(republican == 1) %>% drop_na(weight)
dem_data <- main_2024 %>% filter(democrat == 1) %>% drop_na(weight)

cat("=== PARTISAN-MODERATED: Right-leaning Untrustworthy ===\n\n")

# % Exposed to Right-leaning: Rep vs Dem
for (party_label in c("Republican", "Democrat")) {
  d <- if (party_label == "Republican") rep_data else dem_data
  m <- diagis::weighted_mean(x = d$right_untrustworthy_flag, w = d$weight) * 100
  se <- diagis::weighted_se(x = d$right_untrustworthy_flag, w = d$weight) * 100
  cat(sprintf("  %s: %.1f%% exposed (95%% CI [%.1f%%, %.1f%%]), n=%d\n",
              party_label, m, m - 1.96*se, m + 1.96*se, nrow(d)))

  # Visits among exposed
  exposed <- d %>% filter(right_untrustworthy_flag == 1)
  if (nrow(exposed) > 2) {
    m_vis <- diagis::weighted_mean(x = exposed$right_untrustworthy_n, w = exposed$weight)
    se_vis <- diagis::weighted_se(x = exposed$right_untrustworthy_n, w = exposed$weight)
    cat(sprintf("    Visits among exposed: %.1f (95%% CI [%.1f, %.1f]), n=%d\n",
                m_vis, m_vis - 1.96*se_vis, m_vis + 1.96*se_vis, nrow(exposed)))
  }

  # % of news visits
  m_news <- diagis::weighted_mean(x = d$pct_news_right_untrustworthy, w = d$weight) * 100
  se_news <- diagis::weighted_se(x = d$pct_news_right_untrustworthy, w = d$weight) * 100
  cat(sprintf("    %% of news visits: %.2f%% (95%% CI [%.2f%%, %.2f%%])\n",
              m_news, m_news - 1.96*se_news, m_news + 1.96*se_news))
}

# T-test: Right-leaning exposure, Rep vs Dem
t_right <- weights::wtd.t.test(
  x = rep_data$right_untrustworthy_flag, weight = rep_data$weight,
  y = dem_data$right_untrustworthy_flag, weighty = dem_data$weight
)

sd_rep_r <- sqrt(Hmisc::wtd.var(x = rep_data$right_untrustworthy_flag, weights = rep_data$weight))
sd_dem_r <- sqrt(Hmisc::wtd.var(x = dem_data$right_untrustworthy_flag, weights = dem_data$weight))
pooled_sd_r <- sqrt((sd_rep_r^2 + sd_dem_r^2) / 2)
d_right <- t_right$additional["Difference"] / pooled_sd_r

cat(sprintf("\nT-test (Right-leaning, Rep vs Dem): t(%.0f) = %.2f, p = %.4f, Cohen's d = %.2f\n",
    t_right$coefficients["df"], t_right$coefficients["t.value"], t_right$coefficients["p.value"], d_right))

cat("\n=== PARTISAN-MODERATED: Left-leaning Untrustworthy ===\n\n")

# % Exposed to Left-leaning: Rep vs Dem
for (party_label in c("Republican", "Democrat")) {
  d <- if (party_label == "Republican") rep_data else dem_data
  m <- diagis::weighted_mean(x = d$left_untrustworthy_flag, w = d$weight) * 100
  se <- diagis::weighted_se(x = d$left_untrustworthy_flag, w = d$weight) * 100
  cat(sprintf("  %s: %.1f%% exposed (95%% CI [%.1f%%, %.1f%%]), n=%d\n",
              party_label, m, m - 1.96*se, m + 1.96*se, nrow(d)))

  # Visits among exposed
  exposed <- d %>% filter(left_untrustworthy_flag == 1)
  if (nrow(exposed) > 2) {
    m_vis <- diagis::weighted_mean(x = exposed$left_untrustworthy_n, w = exposed$weight)
    se_vis <- diagis::weighted_se(x = exposed$left_untrustworthy_n, w = exposed$weight)
    cat(sprintf("    Visits among exposed: %.1f (95%% CI [%.1f, %.1f]), n=%d\n",
                m_vis, m_vis - 1.96*se_vis, m_vis + 1.96*se_vis, nrow(exposed)))
  }

  # % of news visits
  m_news <- diagis::weighted_mean(x = d$pct_news_left_untrustworthy, w = d$weight) * 100
  se_news <- diagis::weighted_se(x = d$pct_news_left_untrustworthy, w = d$weight) * 100
  cat(sprintf("    %% of news visits: %.2f%% (95%% CI [%.2f%%, %.2f%%])\n",
              m_news, m_news - 1.96*se_news, m_news + 1.96*se_news))
}

# T-test: Left-leaning exposure, Rep vs Dem
t_left <- weights::wtd.t.test(
  x = rep_data$left_untrustworthy_flag, weight = rep_data$weight,
  y = dem_data$left_untrustworthy_flag, weighty = dem_data$weight
)

sd_rep_l <- sqrt(Hmisc::wtd.var(x = rep_data$left_untrustworthy_flag, weights = rep_data$weight))
sd_dem_l <- sqrt(Hmisc::wtd.var(x = dem_data$left_untrustworthy_flag, weights = dem_data$weight))
pooled_sd_l <- sqrt((sd_rep_l^2 + sd_dem_l^2) / 2)
d_left <- t_left$additional["Difference"] / pooled_sd_l

cat(sprintf("\nT-test (Left-leaning, Rep vs Dem): t(%.0f) = %.2f, p = %.4f, Cohen's d = %.2f\n",
    t_left$coefficients["df"], t_left$coefficients["t.value"], t_left$coefficients["p.value"], d_left))

# T-test: % of news visits to Right-leaning, Rep vs Dem
t_news_r <- weights::wtd.t.test(
  x = rep_data$pct_news_right_untrustworthy, weight = rep_data$weight,
  y = dem_data$pct_news_right_untrustworthy, weighty = dem_data$weight
)
sd_rep_nr <- sqrt(Hmisc::wtd.var(x = rep_data$pct_news_right_untrustworthy, weights = rep_data$weight))
sd_dem_nr <- sqrt(Hmisc::wtd.var(x = dem_data$pct_news_right_untrustworthy, weights = dem_data$weight))
pooled_sd_nr <- sqrt((sd_rep_nr^2 + sd_dem_nr^2) / 2)
d_news_r <- t_news_r$additional["Difference"] / pooled_sd_nr

cat(sprintf("\nT-test (%% news Right-leaning, Rep vs Dem): t(%.0f) = %.2f, p = %.4f, Cohen's d = %.2f\n",
    t_news_r$coefficients["df"], t_news_r$coefficients["t.value"], t_news_r$coefficients["p.value"], d_news_r))

# T-test: % of news visits to Left-leaning, Rep vs Dem
t_news_l <- weights::wtd.t.test(
  x = rep_data$pct_news_left_untrustworthy, weight = rep_data$weight,
  y = dem_data$pct_news_left_untrustworthy, weighty = dem_data$weight
)
sd_rep_nl <- sqrt(Hmisc::wtd.var(x = rep_data$pct_news_left_untrustworthy, weights = rep_data$weight))
sd_dem_nl <- sqrt(Hmisc::wtd.var(x = dem_data$pct_news_left_untrustworthy, weights = dem_data$weight))
pooled_sd_nl <- sqrt((sd_rep_nl^2 + sd_dem_nl^2) / 2)
d_news_l <- t_news_l$additional["Difference"] / pooled_sd_nl

cat(sprintf("\nT-test (%% news Left-leaning, Rep vs Dem): t(%.0f) = %.2f, p = %.4f, Cohen's d = %.2f\n",
    t_news_l$coefficients["df"], t_news_l$coefficients["t.value"], t_news_l$coefficients["p.value"], d_news_l))
```

```{r ideology_composition_figure, fig.width=12, fig.height=5}
# ============================================================
# FIGURE: 3 dodged pointrange panels (A/B/C)
# x = domain ideology, color = party, dodged
# ============================================================

ideology_colors <- c("Right-leaning" = "#F39B7FFF", "Left-leaning" = "#3C5488FF")

# ---- Build data for all 3 panels (4 cells: 2 parties × 2 ideologies) ----
panel_data <- list()
for (party_label in c("Republicans", "Democrats")) {
  d <- if (party_label == "Republicans") rep_data else dem_data
  for (ideo in c("Right-leaning", "Left-leaning")) {
    ideo_lower <- tolower(sub("-leaning", "", ideo))
    flag_col <- paste0(ideo_lower, "_untrustworthy_flag")
    n_col <- paste0(ideo_lower, "_untrustworthy_n")
    pct_col <- paste0("pct_news_", ideo_lower, "_untrustworthy")

    # Panel A: % exposed (full party sample)
    m_exp <- diagis::weighted_mean(x = d[[flag_col]], w = d$weight)
    se_exp <- diagis::weighted_se(x = d[[flag_col]], w = d$weight)

    # Panel B: among exposed only
    exposed <- d %>% filter(!!sym(flag_col) == 1)
    if (nrow(exposed) > 1) {
      m_vis <- diagis::weighted_mean(x = exposed[[n_col]], w = exposed$weight)
      se_vis <- diagis::weighted_se(x = exposed[[n_col]], w = exposed$weight)
      m_pct <- diagis::weighted_mean(x = exposed[[pct_col]], w = exposed$weight)
      se_pct <- diagis::weighted_se(x = exposed[[pct_col]], w = exposed$weight)
    } else {
      m_vis <- NA; se_vis <- NA; m_pct <- NA; se_pct <- NA
    }

    panel_data[[length(panel_data) + 1]] <- tibble(
      party = party_label, domain_ideology = ideo, n_exposed = nrow(exposed),
      exp_mean = m_exp, exp_se = se_exp,
      vis_mean = m_vis, vis_se = se_vis,
      pct_mean = m_pct, pct_se = se_pct
    )
  }
}
panel_df <- bind_rows(panel_data)

# ---- Panel A: % Exposed ----
panel_a_df <- panel_df %>%
  transmute(party, domain_ideology,
            mean = exp_mean, low = exp_mean - 1.96 * exp_se, high = exp_mean + 1.96 * exp_se)

       aes(x = party, y = mean, ymin = low, ymax = high, color = domain_ideology)) +
  geom_pointrange(position = position_dodge(width = 0.5), size = 0.8, fatten = 2) +

       title = "A",

  theme_bw() +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
        legend.position = "bottom")

# ---- Panel B: Visits among exposed ----
panel_b_df <- panel_df %>%
  filter(!is.na(vis_mean)) %>%

            mean = vis_mean, low = vis_mean - 1.96 * vis_se, high = vis_mean + 1.96 * vis_se)

panel_b <- ggplot(panel_b_df,

# ---- Panel C: % of news visits (FULL sample, not among exposed) ----

    party = "Democrats", domain_ideology = "Right-leaning"
  ),

    party = "Democrats", domain_ideology = "Left-leaning"
  )
) %>%
  mutate(low = mean - 1.96 * se, high = mean + 1.96 * se)

panel_c <- ggplot(panel_c_df,
```

# 6. Exploratory Analyses

## 6.1 Credible News Consumption
This section compares consumption of credible news sources between 2020 and 2024 elections, using the same database as used in the 2020 study.

### 6.1.1 Exposure Patterns to Credible News

```{r credible_exposure_calculations}
# Calculate 2024 exposure rate with weighted mean and standard error
credible_exposure_2024 <- tibble(
  mean = diagis::weighted_mean(
    x = main_2024$hard_news_flag,
    w = main_2024$weight),
  se = diagis::weighted_se(
    x = main_2024$hard_news_flag,
    w = main_2024$weight)
) %>%
mutate(
  low = mean - se * 1.96,
  high = mean + se * 1.96,
  year = "2024"
)

# Calculate 2020 exposure rate
credible_exposure_2020 <- tibble(
  mean = diagis::weighted_mean(
    x = main_2020$hard_news_flag,
    w = main_2020$weight),
  se = diagis::weighted_se(
    x = main_2020$hard_news_flag,
    w = main_2020$weight)
) %>%
mutate(
  low = mean - se * 1.96,
  high = mean + se * 1.96,
  year = "2020"
)

# Calculate absolute difference
credible_abs_diff <- credible_exposure_2024$mean - credible_exposure_2020$mean
credible_abs_diff_se <- sqrt(credible_exposure_2024$se^2 + credible_exposure_2020$se^2)
credible_abs_diff_ci_low <- credible_abs_diff - 1.96 * credible_abs_diff_se
credible_abs_diff_ci_high <- credible_abs_diff + 1.96 * credible_abs_diff_se

# Calculate relative risk
credible_relative_risk <- credible_exposure_2024$mean / credible_exposure_2020$mean
# Delta method for CI of ratio
credible_ratio_se <- credible_relative_risk * 
  sqrt((credible_exposure_2024$se/credible_exposure_2024$mean)^2 + 
       (credible_exposure_2020$se/credible_exposure_2020$mean)^2)
credible_ratio_ci_low <- credible_relative_risk - 1.96 * credible_ratio_se
credible_ratio_ci_high <- credible_relative_risk + 1.96 * credible_ratio_se

# Perform weighted t-test
credible_exposure_diff <- weights::wtd.t.test(
  x = main_2024$hard_news_flag,
  weight = main_2024$weight,
  y = main_2020$hard_news_flag,
  weighty = main_2020$weight
)

# Calculate Cohen's d
sd_credible_2024 <- sqrt(Hmisc::wtd.var(
  x = main_2024$hard_news_flag,
  weights = main_2024$weight
))

sd_credible_2020 <- sqrt(Hmisc::wtd.var(
  x = main_2020$hard_news_flag,
  weights = main_2020$weight
))

sd_pooled_credible <- sqrt((sd_credible_2024^2 + sd_credible_2020^2) / 2)
cohens_d_credible <- (credible_exposure_diff$additional[["Mean.x"]] - 
                      credible_exposure_diff$additional[["Mean.y"]]) / sd_pooled_credible

# Create comprehensive statistical table
credible_exposure_stats <- tibble(
  Measure = c("2024 Exposure Rate", "2020 Exposure Rate", "Absolute Difference",
              "Relative Risk", "Cohen's d", "df", "t-statistic", "p-value"),
  Value = c(
    paste0(scales::percent(credible_exposure_2024$mean, accuracy = 0.1),
           " (95% CI: [", scales::percent(credible_exposure_2024$low, accuracy = 0.1),
           ", ", scales::percent(credible_exposure_2024$high, accuracy = 0.1), "])"),
    paste0(scales::percent(credible_exposure_2020$mean, accuracy = 0.1),
           " (95% CI: [", scales::percent(credible_exposure_2020$low, accuracy = 0.1),
           ", ", scales::percent(credible_exposure_2020$high, accuracy = 0.1), "])"),
    paste0(scales::percent(credible_abs_diff, accuracy = 0.1),
           " (95% CI: [", scales::percent(credible_abs_diff_ci_low, accuracy = 0.1),
           ", ", scales::percent(credible_abs_diff_ci_high, accuracy = 0.1), "])"),
    paste0(round(credible_relative_risk, 2),
           "x (95% CI: [", round(credible_ratio_ci_low, 2),
           ", ", round(credible_ratio_ci_high, 2), "])"),
    as.character(round(cohens_d_credible, 3)),
    as.character(round(credible_exposure_diff$coefficients["df"], 0)),
    as.character(round(credible_exposure_diff$coefficients[1], 2)),
    format.pval(credible_exposure_diff$coefficients[3], digits = 3)
  )
)

# Print table
knitr::kable(credible_exposure_stats, 
             caption = "Credible News Exposure Statistics",
             align = c("l", "r"))
```

```{r credible_exposure_visualization}
# Combine data for visualization
credible_exposure_combined <- bind_rows(credible_exposure_2024, credible_exposure_2020)

# Create comparison plot
ggplot(credible_exposure_combined, 
       aes(x = year, y = mean, ymin = low, ymax = high)) +
  geom_pointrange(color = "black") +

                    breaks = seq(0, 1, .2),
                    limits = c(0, max(credible_exposure_combined$high) * 1.1)) +
  labs(x = "Election Year",
       y = "Percentage Exposed to Credible News Websites",
       title = "") +

  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.major = element_blank())

# Save the plot
ggsave("../figures/credible-news-proportion.pdf", width = 5, height = 5)
```

```{r credible_visit_frequency}
# Calculate visit frequency among exposed users
# Filter for exposed users only
exposed_credible_2024 <- main_2024 %>% filter(hard_news_flag == 1)
exposed_credible_2020 <- main_2020 %>% filter(hard_news_flag == 1)

# Calculate weighted means for visit counts among exposed
credible_visits_2024 <- tibble(
  mean = diagis::weighted_mean(
    x = exposed_credible_2024$hard_news_n,
    w = exposed_credible_2024$weight),
  se = diagis::weighted_se(
    x = exposed_credible_2024$hard_news_n,
    w = exposed_credible_2024$weight)
) %>%
mutate(
  low = mean - se * 1.96,
  high = mean + se * 1.96,
  year = "2024"
)

credible_visits_2020 <- tibble(
  mean = diagis::weighted_mean(
    x = exposed_credible_2020$hard_news_n,
    w = exposed_credible_2020$weight),
  se = diagis::weighted_se(
    x = exposed_credible_2020$hard_news_n,
    w = exposed_credible_2020$weight)
) %>%
mutate(
  low = mean - se * 1.96,
  high = mean + se * 1.96,
  year = "2020"
)

# Statistical comparison of visit counts
credible_visits_diff <- weights::wtd.t.test(
  x = exposed_credible_2024$hard_news_n,
  weight = exposed_credible_2024$weight,
  y = exposed_credible_2020$hard_news_n,
  weighty = exposed_credible_2020$weight
)

# Calculate Cohen's d for visit frequency
sd_visits_2024 <- sqrt(Hmisc::wtd.var(
  x = exposed_credible_2024$hard_news_n,
  weights = exposed_credible_2024$weight
))

sd_visits_2020 <- sqrt(Hmisc::wtd.var(
  x = exposed_credible_2020$hard_news_n,
  weights = exposed_credible_2020$weight
))

sd_pooled_visits <- sqrt((sd_visits_2024^2 + sd_visits_2020^2) / 2)
cohens_d_visits <- (credible_visits_diff$additional[["Mean.x"]] - 
                    credible_visits_diff$additional[["Mean.y"]]) / sd_pooled_visits

# Create results table for visit frequency
credible_visits_stats <- tibble(
  Measure = c("2024 Average Visits", "2020 Average Visits", "Absolute Difference",
              "Cohen's d", "df", "t-statistic", "p-value"),
  Value = c(
    paste0(round(credible_visits_2024$mean, 1),
           " (95% CI: [", round(credible_visits_2024$low, 1),
           ", ", round(credible_visits_2024$high, 1), "])"),
    paste0(round(credible_visits_2020$mean, 1),
           " (95% CI: [", round(credible_visits_2020$low, 1),
           ", ", round(credible_visits_2020$high, 1), "])"),
    paste0(round(credible_visits_2024$mean - credible_visits_2020$mean, 1),
           " (95% CI: [",
           round(credible_visits_2024$mean - credible_visits_2020$mean -
                 1.96 * sqrt(credible_visits_2024$se^2 + credible_visits_2020$se^2), 1),
           ", ",
           round(credible_visits_2024$mean - credible_visits_2020$mean +
                 1.96 * sqrt(credible_visits_2024$se^2 + credible_visits_2020$se^2), 1),
           "])"),
    as.character(round(cohens_d_visits, 3)),
    as.character(round(credible_visits_diff$coefficients["df"], 0)),
    as.character(round(credible_visits_diff$coefficients[1], 2)),
    format.pval(credible_visits_diff$coefficients[3], digits = 3)
  )
)

# Print visit frequency table
knitr::kable(credible_visits_stats, 
             caption = "Credible News Visit Frequency Statistics (Among Exposed Users)",
             align = c("l", "r"))
```

```{r topic_data_load}
# Load topic-level person dataset produced by data engineering
topic_exposure_2024 <- readRDS("../data/topic-exposure-2024.rds")

# Verify structure
stopifnot(all(c("caseid", "weight", "topic", "domain_type", "topic_flag", "topic_n") %in% names(topic_exposure_2024)))
cat(sprintf("Loaded %d rows: %d participants × %d topics × %d domain types\n",
            nrow(topic_exposure_2024),
            n_distinct(topic_exposure_2024$caseid),
            n_distinct(topic_exposure_2024$topic),
            n_distinct(topic_exposure_2024$domain_type)))
```

```{r topic_exposure_metrics}
# Compute weighted exposure metrics for each topic × domain_type
# Uses group_modify for safe handling of small cells
compute_topic_metrics <- function(df, ...) {
  exposed <- df %>% filter(topic_flag == 1)
  tibble(
    pct_exposed = diagis::weighted_mean(x = df$topic_flag, w = df$weight),
    pct_exposed_se = diagis::weighted_se(x = df$topic_flag, w = df$weight),
    n_exposed = nrow(exposed),
    n_total = nrow(df),
    visits_mean = if (nrow(exposed) >= 5) diagis::weighted_mean(x = exposed$topic_n, w = exposed$weight) else NA_real_,
    visits_se = if (nrow(exposed) >= 5) diagis::weighted_se(x = exposed$topic_n, w = exposed$weight) else NA_real_
  )
}

topic_metrics <- topic_exposure_2024 %>%
  group_by(topic, domain_type) %>%
  group_modify(compute_topic_metrics) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(
    pct_exposed_low = pct_exposed - 1.96 * pct_exposed_se,
    pct_exposed_high = pct_exposed + 1.96 * pct_exposed_se,
    visits_low = visits_mean - 1.96 * visits_se,
    visits_high = visits_mean + 1.96 * visits_se
  )

# Display untrustworthy topic metrics
cat("\nUntrustworthy exposure by topic (weighted):\n")
topic_metrics %>%
  filter(domain_type == "untrustworthy") %>%
  arrange(desc(pct_exposed)) %>%
  transmute(topic,
            pct = sprintf("%.1f%% (95%% CI [%.1f%%, %.1f%%])",
                         pct_exposed * 100, pct_exposed_low * 100, pct_exposed_high * 100),
            n_exposed,
            visits = sprintf("%.1f (95%% CI [%.1f, %.1f])",
                           visits_mean, visits_low, visits_high)) %>%
  print(n = 25)

# Display credible news topic metrics
cat("\nCredible news exposure by topic (weighted):\n")
topic_metrics %>%
  filter(domain_type == "hard_news") %>%
  arrange(desc(pct_exposed)) %>%
  transmute(topic,
            pct = sprintf("%.1f%% (95%% CI [%.1f%%, %.1f%%])",
                         pct_exposed * 100, pct_exposed_low * 100, pct_exposed_high * 100),
            n_exposed,
            visits = sprintf("%.1f (95%% CI [%.1f, %.1f])",
                           visits_mean, visits_low, visits_high)) %>%
  print(n = 25)
```

```{r topic_share_figure, fig.width=10, fig.height=7}
# Topic shares — what % of credible news / untrustworthy visits go to each topic?
# For each person × domain_type: topic_n / total visits to that domain_type
# Weighted mean across all exposed participants

# Compute person-level totals for each domain_type
person_totals <- topic_exposure_2024 %>%
  filter(domain_type %in% c("hard_news", "untrustworthy")) %>%
  group_by(caseid, domain_type) %>%
  summarise(total_domain_visits = sum(topic_n), .groups = "drop")

# Join back to get topic shares
topic_shares <- topic_exposure_2024 %>%
  filter(domain_type %in% c("hard_news", "untrustworthy")) %>%
  inner_join(person_totals, by = c("caseid", "domain_type")) %>%
  mutate(topic_share = ifelse(total_domain_visits > 0, topic_n / total_domain_visits, 0))

# Compute weighted mean share per topic × domain_type (among exposed to that domain_type)
topic_share_metrics <- topic_shares %>%
  filter(total_domain_visits > 0) %>%
  group_by(topic, domain_type) %>%
  summarise(
    share_mean = diagis::weighted_mean(x = topic_share, w = weight),
    share_se = diagis::weighted_se(x = topic_share, w = weight),
    n_exposed = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    share_low = share_mean - 1.96 * share_se,
    share_high = share_mean + 1.96 * share_se,
    domain_type_label = factor(
      ifelse(domain_type == "hard_news", "Credible News", "Untrustworthy"),
      levels = c("Credible News", "Untrustworthy")
    )
  )

cat("\nTopic share of consumption (among exposed):\n")
topic_share_metrics %>%
  arrange(domain_type, desc(share_mean)) %>%
  transmute(domain_type, topic,
            share = sprintf("%.1f%% [%.1f%%, %.1f%%]", share_mean * 100, share_low * 100, share_high * 100),
            n_exposed) %>%
  print(n = 50)

# Figure: Topic shares — same style as topic_composition_figure

type_colors <- c("Credible News" = npg_all[6], "Untrustworthy" = npg_all[7])

topic_share_metrics <- topic_share_metrics %>%
  mutate(topic = factor(topic, levels = topic_share_order))

topic_share_figure <- ggplot(topic_share_metrics,
       aes(x = topic, y = share_mean * 100, ymin = share_low * 100,

        legend.text = element_text(size = 10))

print(topic_share_figure)
ggsave("../figures/topic_share_of_consumption.pdf", topic_share_figure, width = 14, height = 8)
```

```{r behavioral_overlap_analysis}
# Behavioral overlap — are hard news and untrustworthy consumers the same people?

# Part A: Aggregate 2x2 co-exposure cross-tab
co_exposure_2x2 <- main_2024 %>%
  mutate(
    profile = case_when(
      hard_news_flag == 1 & untrustworthy_flag == 1 ~ "Both",
      hard_news_flag == 1 & untrustworthy_flag == 0 ~ "Credible Only",
      hard_news_flag == 0 & untrustworthy_flag == 1 ~ "Untrustworthy Only",
      TRUE ~ "Neither"
    )
  )

# Weighted proportions for each profile
profile_stats <- co_exposure_2x2 %>%
  group_by(profile) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    weighted_pct = diagis::weighted_mean(x = rep(1, n()), w = weight) * 0, # placeholder
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Compute weighted proportions properly
for (p in c("Both", "Credible Only", "Untrustworthy Only", "Neither")) {
  indicator <- as.integer(co_exposure_2x2$profile == p)
  profile_stats$weighted_pct[profile_stats$profile == p] <-
    diagis::weighted_mean(x = indicator, w = co_exposure_2x2$weight)
  profile_stats$weighted_se[profile_stats$profile == p] <-
    diagis::weighted_se(x = indicator, w = co_exposure_2x2$weight)
}

profile_stats <- profile_stats %>%
  mutate(
    pct_low = weighted_pct - 1.96 * weighted_se,
    pct_high = weighted_pct + 1.96 * weighted_se
  )

cat("\n2x2 Co-exposure profile (weighted):\n")
print(profile_stats %>%
  transmute(Profile = profile, n,
            `Weighted %` = sprintf("%.1f%% [%.1f%%, %.1f%%]",
                                   weighted_pct * 100, pct_low * 100, pct_high * 100)))

# Conditional rates
# Of those exposed to untrustworthy, what % also visited credible news?
exposed_untrust <- main_2024 %>% filter(untrustworthy_flag == 1)
cond_untrust_to_credible <- diagis::weighted_mean(
  x = exposed_untrust$hard_news_flag, w = exposed_untrust$weight)
cond_untrust_to_credible_se <- diagis::weighted_se(
  x = exposed_untrust$hard_news_flag, w = exposed_untrust$weight)

# Of those exposed to credible news, what % also visited untrustworthy?
exposed_credible <- main_2024 %>% filter(hard_news_flag == 1)
cond_credible_to_untrust <- diagis::weighted_mean(
  x = exposed_credible$untrustworthy_flag, w = exposed_credible$weight)
cond_credible_to_untrust_se <- diagis::weighted_se(
  x = exposed_credible$untrustworthy_flag, w = exposed_credible$weight)

cat(sprintf("\nOf untrustworthy-exposed: %.1f%% also visited credible news (95%% CI [%.1f%%, %.1f%%])\n",
  cond_untrust_to_credible * 100,
  (cond_untrust_to_credible - 1.96 * cond_untrust_to_credible_se) * 100,
  (cond_untrust_to_credible + 1.96 * cond_untrust_to_credible_se) * 100))
cat(sprintf("Of credible-news-exposed: %.1f%% also visited untrustworthy (95%% CI [%.1f%%, %.1f%%])\n",
  cond_credible_to_untrust * 100,
  (cond_credible_to_untrust - 1.96 * cond_credible_to_untrust_se) * 100,
  (cond_credible_to_untrust + 1.96 * cond_credible_to_untrust_se) * 100))
```

```{r topic_coexposure}
# Part B: Topic-level co-exposure rates
# For each topic: weighted % who visited BOTH hard_news and untrustworthy domains with that topic

# Reshape to wide: one row per person x topic, with flags for each domain_type
topic_wide <- topic_exposure_2024 %>%
  filter(domain_type %in% c("hard_news", "untrustworthy")) %>%
  select(caseid, weight, topic, domain_type, topic_flag) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = domain_type,
    values_from = topic_flag,
    values_fill = 0L
  )

# For each topic, compute co-exposure rate
topic_coexposure <- topic_wide %>%
  mutate(both_flag = as.integer(hard_news > 0 & untrustworthy > 0)) %>%
  group_by(topic) %>%
  summarise(
    co_exposure_rate = diagis::weighted_mean(x = both_flag, w = weight),
    co_exposure_se = diagis::weighted_se(x = both_flag, w = weight),
    n_both = sum(both_flag),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    co_exposure_low = co_exposure_rate - 1.96 * co_exposure_se,
    co_exposure_high = co_exposure_rate + 1.96 * co_exposure_se
  ) %>%
  filter(topic != "Unclassified")  # drop Unclassified, keep all classified topics

cat("\nTopic-level co-exposure rates (credible news AND untrustworthy):\n")
topic_coexposure %>%
  arrange(desc(co_exposure_rate)) %>%
  transmute(topic,
            rate = sprintf("%.1f%% (95%% CI [%.1f%%, %.1f%%])",
                          co_exposure_rate * 100, co_exposure_low * 100, co_exposure_high * 100),
            n_both) %>%
  print(n = 25)
```

```{r topic_correlation_heatmap, fig.width=11, fig.height=9}
# Figure: Correlation heatmap — untrustworthy topics × credible news topics

# Pivot to wide: one row per participant, columns = domain_type_topic
untrust_wide <- topic_exposure_2024 %>%
  filter(domain_type == "untrustworthy") %>%
  select(caseid, topic, topic_n) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = topic, values_from = topic_n, names_prefix = "untrust_")

hardnews_wide <- topic_exposure_2024 %>%
  filter(domain_type == "hard_news") %>%
  select(caseid, topic, topic_n) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = topic, values_from = topic_n, names_prefix = "hn_")

# Join and add weights
cor_data <- untrust_wide %>%
  inner_join(hardnews_wide, by = "caseid") %>%
  inner_join(main_2024 %>% select(caseid, weight), by = "caseid")

# Get topic names
untrust_topics <- sort(unique(topic_exposure_2024$topic[topic_exposure_2024$domain_type == "untrustworthy"]))
hn_topics <- sort(unique(topic_exposure_2024$topic[topic_exposure_2024$domain_type == "hard_news"]))

# Compute weighted correlations using weights::wtd.cor
cor_matrix <- matrix(NA, nrow = length(untrust_topics), ncol = length(hn_topics),
                     dimnames = list(untrust_topics, hn_topics))

for (i in seq_along(untrust_topics)) {
  for (j in seq_along(hn_topics)) {
    x_col <- paste0("untrust_", untrust_topics[i])
    y_col <- paste0("hn_", hn_topics[j])
    if (x_col %in% names(cor_data) & y_col %in% names(cor_data)) {
      x_vals <- cor_data[[x_col]]
      y_vals <- cor_data[[y_col]]
      if (sd(x_vals, na.rm = TRUE) > 0 & sd(y_vals, na.rm = TRUE) > 0) {
        cor_result <- weights::wtd.cor(x_vals, y_vals, weight = cor_data$weight)
        cor_matrix[i, j] <- cor_result[1, 1]
      } else {
        cor_matrix[i, j] <- 0
      }
    }
  }
}

# Drop Unclassified from both axes
keep_rows <- setdiff(rownames(cor_matrix), "Unclassified")
keep_cols <- setdiff(colnames(cor_matrix), "Unclassified")
cor_matrix_filtered <- cor_matrix[keep_rows, keep_cols, drop = FALSE]

# Set zero correlations to NA so they render as white
cor_matrix_filtered[cor_matrix_filtered == 0] <- NA

# Convert to long format for ggplot
cor_long <- as.data.frame(as.table(cor_matrix_filtered)) %>%
  rename(untrustworthy_topic = Var1, credible_news_topic = Var2, correlation = Freq) %>%
  mutate(
    untrustworthy_topic = str_wrap(as.character(untrustworthy_topic), width = 20),
    credible_news_topic = str_wrap(as.character(credible_news_topic), width = 20)
  )

# Same alphabetical topic order on both axes
all_topic_labels <- sort(unique(c(
  as.character(cor_long$untrustworthy_topic),
  as.character(cor_long$credible_news_topic)
)))

cor_long <- cor_long %>%
  mutate(
    untrustworthy_topic = factor(untrustworthy_topic, levels = rev(all_topic_labels)),
    credible_news_topic = factor(credible_news_topic, levels = all_topic_labels)
  )

heatmap_figure <- ggplot(cor_long, aes(x = credible_news_topic, y = untrustworthy_topic,
                                        fill = correlation)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 0.3) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#4DBBD5FF", mid = "white", high = "#E64B35FF",
                       midpoint = 0, limits = c(-0.15, 0.65),
                       na.value = "white",
                       name = "Weighted\nCorrelation") +
  labs(x = "Credible News Topic", y = "Untrustworthy Topic") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
        axis.text.x = element_text(size = 10, angle = 45, hjust = 1),
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10),
        axis.title.x = element_text(size = 11),
        axis.title.y = element_text(size = 11),
        legend.text = element_text(size = 10),
        legend.title = element_text(size = 11))

print(heatmap_figure)
ggsave("../figures/topic_correlation_heatmap.pdf", heatmap_figure, width = 11, height = 9)

# Extract full correlation stats (r, SE, t, p, CI) for key pairs cited in SM text
key_pairs <- list(
  c("Political news or commentary", "Political news or commentary"),
  c("General News", "General News"),
  c("Health or medical information", "Health or medical information"),
  c("Conspiracy theories or hoaxes", "Political news or commentary"),
  c("Health or medical information", "Political news or commentary")
)

n_cor <- nrow(cor_data)
cat("\n=== Key correlation pairs ===\n")
for (pair in key_pairs) {
  x_col <- paste0("untrust_", pair[1])
  y_col <- paste0("hn_", pair[2])
  r_result <- weights::wtd.cor(cor_data[[x_col]], cor_data[[y_col]], weight = cor_data$weight)
  r <- r_result[1, "correlation"]
  t_val <- r_result[1, "t.value"]
  p_val <- r_result[1, "p.value"]
  # Fisher z-transform for 95% CI
  z <- atanh(r)
  z_se <- 1 / sqrt(n_cor - 3)
  r_low <- tanh(z - 1.96 * z_se)
  r_high <- tanh(z + 1.96 * z_se)
  cor_df <- n_cor - 2
  cat(sprintf("Untrust %-35s x Cred %-35s  r = %.2f, 95%% CI [%.2f, %.2f], t(%d) = %.2f, P = %.3f\n",
    pair[1], pair[2], r, r_low, r_high, cor_df, t_val, p_val))
}
```

```{r credible_news_demographics, results='asis'}
# Force float barrier before analysis
cat("\\FloatBarrier\n")

# 2020 model (baseline, using age_ variables)
model_credible_2020 <- lm(
  hard_news_flag ~ republican + political_interest + 
    college + female + non_white + 
    age_30_44 + age_45_64 + age_65_plus,  # age_18_29 is reference
  data = main_2020,
  weights = weight
)

# 2024 model (using age_ variables)
model_credible_2024 <- lm(
  hard_news_flag ~ republican + political_interest + 
    college + female + non_white + 
    age_30_44 + age_45_64 + age_65_plus,  # age_18_29 is reference
  data = main_2024,
  weights = weight
)

# Get coefficients, SEs, p-values, and CIs for credible news models
coef_2020 <- summary(model_credible_2020)$coefficients
ci_2020 <- confint(model_credible_2020)
coef_2024 <- summary(model_credible_2024)$coefficients
ci_2024 <- confint(model_credible_2024)

# Create the table content as text - exactly matching the Nature paper format
cat("\\begin{table}[ht]\n")
cat("\\caption{Who chooses to visit credible news websites}\n")
cat("\\label{tab:credible_model}\n")
cat("\\begin{tabular}{lll}\n")
cat("\\hline\n")
cat(" & \\multicolumn{2}{l}{Exposure to at least one credible news website (binary)} \\\\ \n")
cat("\\cline{2-3}\n")
cat(" & 2020 & 2024 \\\\ \n")
cat("\\hline\n")

# Add variables with alternating shading
format_coef("Trump supporter", "republican", "republican", TRUE)
format_coef("Political interest", "political_interest", "political_interest")
format_coef("College", "college", "college", TRUE)
format_coef("Female", "female", "female")
format_coef("Non-white", "non_white", "non_white", TRUE)
format_coef("Age 30-44 years", "age_30_44", "age_30_44")
format_coef("Age 45-64 years", "age_45_64", "age_45_64", TRUE)
format_coef("Age 65+ years", "age_65_plus", "age_65_plus")
format_coef("Constant", "(Intercept)", "(Intercept)", TRUE)

# Add R² and N with solid line above
cat("\\hline\n")
cat(sprintf("$R^2$ & %.3f & %.3f \\\\ \n", 
           summary(model_credible_2020)$r.squared, 
           summary(model_credible_2024)$r.squared))
cat(sprintf("$N$ & %d & %d \\\\ \n", 
           nrow(model_credible_2020$model), 
           nrow(model_credible_2024$model)))
cat("\\hline\n")
cat("\\end{tabular}\n")
cat("\\end{table}\n")

# Force float barrier after analysis
cat("\\FloatBarrier\n")
```

## 6.3 Technology Attitudes and Digital Term Knowledge

### 6.3.1 Digital Term Knowledge

#### 6.3.1.1 Digital Term Knowledge and Untrustworthy Website Vulnerability

```{r fig.align="center"}
literacy_components <- c("digital_term_adv_search", "digital_term_pdf", "digital_term_spyware", 
                         "digital_term_wiki", "digital_term_cache", "digital_term_phishing")
component_labels <- c("Advanced Search", "PDF", "Spyware", 
                      "Wiki", "Cache", "Phishing")

component_exposure_list <- list()

for(i in seq_along(literacy_components)) {
  comp <- literacy_components[i]
  lab <- component_labels[i]
  
  # Summarize exposure for each distinct score
  comp_data <- main_2024 %>%
    group_by(!!sym(comp)) %>%
    summarise(
      exposure_rate = diagis::weighted_mean(untrustworthy_flag, weight),
      exposure_se   = diagis::weighted_se(untrustworthy_flag, weight),
      n            = n()
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      ci_lower = exposure_rate - 1.96 * exposure_se,
      ci_upper = exposure_rate + 1.96 * exposure_se,
      component = lab
    ) %>%
    rename(score = !!sym(comp))
  
  component_exposure_list[[i]] <- comp_data
}

all_components_exposure <- bind_rows(component_exposure_list)

component_graph <- ggplot(all_components_exposure, aes(x = score, y = exposure_rate)) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = ci_lower, ymax = ci_upper), width = 0.2) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, color = "darkblue") +
  facet_wrap(~ component, scales = "free_x", ncol = 3) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format()) +
  labs(
    x = "Score",
    y = "Percentage Exposed to Untrustworthy Website",
    title = "Digital Literacy Components and 
    Untrustworthy Website Exposure"
  ) +
  theme_classic()
```

```{r results = "asis"}
# Fit individual component models (without demographic controls)
model_adv_search <- lm(untrustworthy_flag ~ digital_term_adv_search, data = main_2024, weights = weight)
model_pdf        <- lm(untrustworthy_flag ~ digital_term_pdf,        data = main_2024, weights = weight)
model_spyware    <- lm(untrustworthy_flag ~ digital_term_spyware,    data = main_2024, weights = weight)
model_wiki       <- lm(untrustworthy_flag ~ digital_term_wiki,       data = main_2024, weights = weight)
model_cache      <- lm(untrustworthy_flag ~ digital_term_cache,      data = main_2024, weights = weight)
model_phishing   <- lm(untrustworthy_flag ~ digital_term_phishing,   data = main_2024, weights = weight)

# Fit composite models
simple_composite_model <- lm(untrustworthy_flag ~ digital_term_knowledge_score,
                             data = main_2024, weights = weight)
full_composite_model   <- lm(untrustworthy_flag ~ digital_term_knowledge_score + republican + political_interest +
                                          college + female + non_white +
                                          age_30_44 + age_45_64 + age_65_plus,
                             data = main_2024, weights = weight)

# Rename models to short names for stargazer
m1 <- model_adv_search
m2 <- model_pdf
m3 <- model_spyware
m4 <- model_wiki
m5 <- model_cache
m6 <- model_phishing
m7 <- simple_composite_model
m8 <- full_composite_model

# Create a single stargazer table for all eight models
stargazer(
  m1, m2, m3, m4, m5, m6, m7, m8,
  type = "latex",
  title = "Digital Literacy Components and Untrustworthy Website Exposure",
  label = "tab:digital_term_knowledge_untrustworthy",
  model.names = FALSE,
  model.numbers = TRUE,
  dep.var.labels = "Untrustworthy Exposure",
  covariate.labels = c(
    "Term: Adv. Search", "Term: PDF", "Term: Spyware",
    "Term: Wiki", "Term: Cache", "Term: Phishing",
    "Composite Digital Literacy", "Republican", "Political Interest",
    "College", "Female", "Non-White", "Age 30-44", 
    "Age 45-64", "Age 65+"
  ),
  omit.stat = c("f", "ser"),
  no.space = TRUE,
  star.cutoffs = c(.05, .01, .001),
         header = FALSE)
```

##### Sensitivity: Digital Literacy Paradox and Visit Volume

```{r results = "asis"}
# Sensitivity analysis: does the digital literacy
# paradox reflect a mechanical volume confound (high-literacy people browse more,
# so they trip the binary untrustworthy_flag more often), or does it survive
# adjustment for total visits?
#
# M1: total_visits ~ literacy                       (does literacy predict volume at all?)
# M2: total_visits ~ literacy + demos               (does it survive demographic adjustment?)
# M3: untrustworthy_flag ~ literacy + total_visits  (does the paradox survive volume control?)
#                         + demos
m_volume_simple <- lm(total_visits ~ digital_term_knowledge_score,
                      data = main_2024, weights = weight)

m_volume_full <- lm(total_visits ~ digital_term_knowledge_score +
                                   republican + political_interest +
                                   college + female + non_white +
                                   age_30_44 + age_45_64 + age_65_plus,
                    data = main_2024, weights = weight)

m_paradox_volctrl <- lm(untrustworthy_flag ~ digital_term_knowledge_score +
                                             total_visits +
                                             republican + political_interest +
                                             college + female + non_white +
                                             age_30_44 + age_45_64 + age_65_plus,
                        data = main_2024, weights = weight)

stargazer(
  m_volume_simple, m_volume_full, m_paradox_volctrl,
  type = "latex",
  title = "Sensitivity of the Digital Literacy Paradox to Visit Volume",
  label = "tab:digital_literacy_volume_sensitivity",
  model.names = FALSE,
  model.numbers = TRUE,
  dep.var.labels = c("Total Visits", "Untrustworthy Exposure"),
  covariate.labels = c(
    "Composite Digital Literacy", "Total Visits", "Republican",
    "Political Interest", "College", "Female", "Non-White",
    "Age 30-44", "Age 45-64", "Age 65+"
  ),
  omit.stat = c("f", "ser"),
  no.space = TRUE,
  star.cutoffs = c(.05, .01, .001),
         header = FALSE)
```

##### Sensitivity: Digital Literacy Paradox and Source Diversity

```{r results = "asis"}
# Sensitivity analysis: does the digital literacy
# paradox reflect a source-diversity confound (high-literacy people visit a more
# diverse set of sources, so they encounter more untrustworthy ones as a
# byproduct)? Mirrors the visit-volume sensitivity (M1/M2/M3) exactly, just
# swapping total_visits for two unique-domain operationalizations:
#
#   Set A — total_unique_domains: distinct domains visited per participant (any
#                                 domain). This is the conservative test: the
#                                 predictor is essentially independent of the DV
#                                 because untrustworthy visits are a tiny share
#                                 of total unique domains for almost every
#                                 participant.
#
#   Set B — listed_unique_domains: distinct domains visited per participant that
#                                  appear in the union of our three classification
#                                  lists (hard news ∪ untrustworthy ∪ AI
#                                  untrustworthy). Closer to a
#                                  "news/information source diversity" framing,
#                                  but the DV (untrustworthy_flag) is mechanically
#                                  bounded by this measure: visited untrustworthy
#                                  domains are part of listed_unique_domains
#                                  itself, inducing a baseline positive
#                                  association with the DV even absent any
#                                  behavioral story. Any literacy effect that
#                                  survives this control is therefore surviving
#                                  a more demanding test, but the diversity
#                                  coefficient itself should not be over-interpreted.
#                                  This caveat is acknowledged in the SM text.
#
# Within each set:
#   M1: <diversity> ~ literacy                              (does literacy predict diversity?)
#   M2: <diversity> ~ literacy + demos                      (survives demographic adjustment?)
#   M3: untrustworthy_flag ~ literacy + <diversity> + demos (paradox survives diversity control?)
# where <diversity> ∈ {total_unique_domains, listed_unique_domains}.

# Set A: total unique domains
m_div_total_simple <- lm(total_unique_domains ~ digital_term_knowledge_score,
                         data = main_2024, weights = weight)

m_div_total_full <- lm(total_unique_domains ~ digital_term_knowledge_score +
                                              republican + political_interest +
                                              college + female + non_white +
                                              age_30_44 + age_45_64 + age_65_plus,
                       data = main_2024, weights = weight)

m_paradox_divtotal <- lm(untrustworthy_flag ~ digital_term_knowledge_score +
                                              total_unique_domains +
                                              republican + political_interest +
                                              college + female + non_white +
                                              age_30_44 + age_45_64 + age_65_plus,
                         data = main_2024, weights = weight)

# Set B: unique domains in our 3 lists
m_div_listed_simple <- lm(listed_unique_domains ~ digital_term_knowledge_score,
                          data = main_2024, weights = weight)

m_div_listed_full <- lm(listed_unique_domains ~ digital_term_knowledge_score +
                                                republican + political_interest +
                                                college + female + non_white +
                                                age_30_44 + age_45_64 + age_65_plus,
                        data = main_2024, weights = weight)

m_paradox_divlisted <- lm(untrustworthy_flag ~ digital_term_knowledge_score +
                                               listed_unique_domains +
                                               republican + political_interest +
                                               college + female + non_white +
                                               age_30_44 + age_45_64 + age_65_plus,
                          data = main_2024, weights = weight)

stargazer(
  m_div_total_simple, m_div_total_full, m_paradox_divtotal,
  type = "latex",
  title = "Sensitivity of the Digital Literacy Paradox to Source Diversity (Total Unique Domains)",
  label = "tab:digital_literacy_diversity_total_sensitivity",
  model.names = FALSE,
  model.numbers = TRUE,
  dep.var.labels = c("Total Unique Domains", "Untrustworthy Exposure"),
  covariate.labels = c(
    "Composite Digital Literacy", "Total Unique Domains", "Republican",
    "Political Interest", "College", "Female", "Non-White",
    "Age 30-44", "Age 45-64", "Age 65+"
  ),
  omit.stat = c("f", "ser"),
  no.space = TRUE,
  star.cutoffs = c(.05, .01, .001),
         header = FALSE)

stargazer(
  m_div_listed_simple, m_div_listed_full, m_paradox_divlisted,
  type = "latex",
  title = "Sensitivity of the Digital Literacy Paradox to Source Diversity (Listed Unique Domains)",
  label = "tab:digital_literacy_diversity_listed_sensitivity",
  model.names = FALSE,
  model.numbers = TRUE,
  dep.var.labels = c("Listed Unique Domains", "Untrustworthy Exposure"),
  covariate.labels = c(
    "Composite Digital Literacy", "Listed Unique Domains", "Republican",
    "Political Interest", "College", "Female", "Non-White",
    "Age 30-44", "Age 45-64", "Age 65+"
  ),
  omit.stat = c("f", "ser"),
  no.space = TRUE,
  star.cutoffs = c(.05, .01, .001),
         header = FALSE)
```


#### 6.3.1.2 Digital Term Knowledge and AI-Generated Untrustworthy Website Exposure

```{r fig.align = "center", fig.height = 8, fig.width = 6}
# Define digital term knowledge component variables and labels
literacy_components <- c("digital_term_adv_search", "digital_term_pdf", "digital_term_spyware", 
                         "digital_term_wiki", "digital_term_cache", "digital_term_phishing")
component_labels   <- c("Advanced Search", "PDF", "Spyware", 
                        "Wiki", "Cache", "Phishing")

# Build a list of data for each component (using ai_untrustworthy_flag)
component_exposure_list_ai <- list()

for(i in seq_along(literacy_components)) {
  comp <- literacy_components[i]
  lab  <- component_labels[i]
  
  comp_data <- main_2024 %>%
    group_by(!!sym(comp)) %>%
    summarise(
      exposure_rate = diagis::weighted_mean(ai_untrustworthy_flag, weight),
      exposure_se   = diagis::weighted_se(ai_untrustworthy_flag, weight),
      n = n()
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      ci_lower = exposure_rate - 1.96 * exposure_se,
      ci_upper = exposure_rate + 1.96 * exposure_se,
      component = lab
    ) %>%
    rename(score = !!sym(comp))
  
  component_exposure_list_ai[[i]] <- comp_data
}

all_components_exposure_ai <- bind_rows(component_exposure_list_ai)

# Create a faceted plot for individual components
component_graph <- ggplot(all_components_exposure_ai, aes(x = score, y = exposure_rate)) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = ci_lower, ymax = ci_upper), width = 0.2) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, color = "darkblue") +
  facet_wrap(~ component, scales = "free_x", ncol = 3) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format()) +
  labs(
    x = "Score",
    y = "Percentage Exposed to AI Untrustworthy Websites",
    title = "Digital Literacy Components and
    AI Untrustworthy Website Exposure"
  ) +
  theme_classic()

# Create a composite plot: Bin digital_term_knowledge_score and plot weighted exposure of ai_untrustworthy_flag
composite_data_ai <- main_2024 %>%
  mutate(digital_literacy_binned = round(digital_term_knowledge_score)) %>%
  group_by(digital_literacy_binned) %>%
  summarise(
    exposure_rate = diagis::weighted_mean(ai_untrustworthy_flag, weight),
    exposure_se   = diagis::weighted_se(ai_untrustworthy_flag, weight),
    n = n()
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    ci_lower = exposure_rate - 1.96 * exposure_se,
    ci_upper = exposure_rate + 1.96 * exposure_se
  )

composite_graph <- ggplot(composite_data_ai, aes(x = digital_literacy_binned, y = exposure_rate)) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = ci_lower, ymax = ci_upper), width = 0.2) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, color = "darkblue") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format()) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, max(composite_data_ai$digital_literacy_binned), by = 1)) +
  labs(
    x = "Digital Literacy Composite Score",
    y = "Percentage Exposed to AI Untrustworthy Websites",
    title = "Digital Literacy Composite Score and
    AI Untrustworthy Website Exposure"
  ) +
  theme_classic()

(component_graph / composite_graph)
```

```{r results = "asis"}
model_speech    <- lm(untrustworthy_flag ~ speech_rec_correct, data = main_2024, weights = weight)

full_composite_model_know   <- lm(untrustworthy_flag ~ ai_knowledge_score + republican + political_interest +
                                          college + female + non_white +
                                          age_30_44 + age_45_64 + age_65_plus,
                                  data = main_2024, weights = weight)

m3 <- model_image
m4 <- model_speech
m5 <- simple_composite_model_know

stargazer(
```

#### 6.3.3.2 AI Knowledge and AI Untrustworthy Websites


```{r fig.align = "center", fig.height = 8, fig.width = 6}
# Build summary data for each AI Knowledge component (outcome = ai_untrustworthy_flag)
component_exposure_list_know_ai <- list()

for(i in seq_along(knowledge_components)) {
  comp <- knowledge_components[i]
  lab  <- knowledge_labels[i]
  
  comp_data <- main_2024 %>%
    filter(!is.na(!!sym(comp))) %>%
    group_by(!!sym(comp)) %>%
    summarise(
      exposure_rate = diagis::weighted_mean(ai_untrustworthy_flag, weight),
      exposure_se   = diagis::weighted_se(ai_untrustworthy_flag, weight),
      n = n()
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      ci_lower = exposure_rate - 1.96 * exposure_se,
      ci_upper = exposure_rate + 1.96 * exposure_se,
      component = lab
    ) %>%
    rename(score = !!sym(comp))
  
  component_exposure_list_know_ai[[i]] <- comp_data
}

all_components_exposure_know_ai <- bind_rows(component_exposure_list_know_ai)

# Faceted plot for individual components (outcome = ai_untrustworthy_flag)
component_graph_know_ai <- ggplot(all_components_exposure_know_ai, aes(x = factor(score), y = exposure_rate)) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = ci_lower, ymax = ci_upper), width = 0.2) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, color = "darkblue", aes(group = 1)) +
  facet_wrap(~ component, scales = "free_x", ncol = 2) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format()) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = c("Incorrect", "Correct")) +
  labs(
    x = "",
    y = "Percentage Exposed to AI-Untrustworthy Website",
    title = "AI Knowledge Components and 
    AI-Untrustworthy Website Exposure"
  ) +
  theme_classic()

# Composite plot using the composite variable ai_knowledge_score (binned) for ai_untrustworthy_flag
composite_data_know_ai <- main_2024 %>%
  mutate(ai_knowledge_binned = round(ai_knowledge_score)) %>%
  group_by(ai_knowledge_binned) %>%
  summarise(
    exposure_rate = diagis::weighted_mean(ai_untrustworthy_flag, weight),
    exposure_se   = diagis::weighted_se(ai_untrustworthy_flag, weight),
    n = n()
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    ci_lower = exposure_rate - 1.96 * exposure_se,
    ci_upper = exposure_rate + 1.96 * exposure_se
  ) %>% 
  filter(!is.na(ai_knowledge_binned))

composite_graph_know_ai <- ggplot(composite_data_know_ai, aes(x = ai_knowledge_binned, y = exposure_rate)) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = ci_lower, ymax = ci_upper), width = 0.2) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, color = "darkblue") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format()) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, max(composite_data_know_ai$ai_knowledge_binned), by = 1)) +
  labs(
    x = "AI Knowledge Composite Score",
    y = "Percentage Exposed to AI-Untrustworthy Website",
    title = "AI Knowledge Composite Score and 
    AI-Untrustworthy Website Exposure"
  ) +
  theme_classic()

(component_graph_know_ai / composite_graph_know_ai)
```

```{r fig.align = "center", fig.height = 8, fig.width = 8}
      exposure_rate = diagis::weighted_mean(ai_untrustworthy_flag, weight),
      exposure_se   = diagis::weighted_se(ai_untrustworthy_flag, weight),
      n = n()
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      ci_lower = exposure_rate - 1.96 * exposure_se,
      ci_upper = exposure_rate + 1.96 * exposure_se,
      component = lab
    ) %>%
    rename(score = !!sym(comp))
  
  attitude_dim_exposure_list_ai[[i]] <- comp_data
}
```

```{r results = "asis"}
# Regression Modeling for Outcome = untrustworthy_flag
```

```{r fig.align = "center", fig.height = 12, fig.width = 8}
    filter(!is.na(!!sym(comp))) %>%
    group_by(!!sym(comp)) %>%
    summarise(
      exposure_rate = diagis::weighted_mean(untrustworthy_flag, weight),
      exposure_se   = diagis::weighted_se(untrustworthy_flag, weight),
      n = n()
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      ci_lower = exposure_rate - 1.96 * exposure_se,
      ci_upper = exposure_rate + 1.96 * exposure_se,
      component = lab
    ) %>%
    rename(score = !!sym(comp))

  component_exposure_list_purpose[[i]] <- comp_data
}

all_components_exposure_purpose <- bind_rows(component_exposure_list_purpose)

# Faceted plot for individual AI usage purpose components (outcome = untrustworthy_flag)
```

# 7. Verasight

"In the weeks around the 2020 U.S. Presidential Election, a past study found that 26.2% of American adults visited at least one "untrustworthy" website (i.e., websites that repeatedly publish false content).

Do you think the percentage of American adults that visited at least one such website in the weeks around the 2024 U.S. Presidential Election was more, less, or the same?"


```{r}
verasight <- read_csv("../data/verasight_survey/2025-026_client.csv")

# Calculate weighted percentages and CIs for overall responses
verasight_overall <- verasight %>%
  filter(!is.na(society_9)) %>%
  mutate(response = case_when(
    society_9 == "1" ~ "More",
    society_9 == "2" ~ "Less",
    society_9 == "3" ~ "Same"
  )) %>%
  group_by(response) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    n_weighted = sum(weight),
    per = n_weighted / sum(verasight$weight[!is.na(verasight$society_9)]),
    se = sqrt((per * (1 - per)) / sum(!is.na(verasight$society_9)))
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    ci_lower = per - 1.96 * se,
    ci_upper = per + 1.96 * se,
    formatted = sprintf("%s (95%% CI: [%s, %s])",
                       scales::percent(per, accuracy = 0.1),
                       scales::percent(ci_lower, accuracy = 0.1),
                       scales::percent(ci_upper, accuracy = 0.1))
  ) %>%
  select(response, formatted)

# Create and display the table
knitr::kable(verasight_overall,
             col.names = c("Response", "Weighted % (95% CI)"),
             caption = "Overall Weighted Responses to 2024 vs 2020 Untrustworthy Website Exposure Question",
             format = "pipe")
```

```{r daily_event_study_data}
# Create event study data with weighted daily exposure rates for 2024
event_study_data_2024 <- daily_exposure_2024 %>%
  filter(party_group %in% c("Republican", "Democrat")) %>%
  group_by(day_relative_to_election, party_group) %>%
  summarise(
    mean = diagis::weighted_mean(x = untrustworthy_flag_daily, w = weight),
    se = diagis::weighted_se(x = untrustworthy_flag_daily, w = weight),
    n = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    percentage = mean * 100,
    ci_lower = (mean - 1.96 * se) * 100,
    ci_upper = (mean + 1.96 * se) * 100,
    year = "2024"
  ) %>% 
  filter(day_relative_to_election <= 6)

# Create event study data with weighted daily exposure rates for 2020
event_study_data_2020 <- daily_exposure_2020 %>%
  filter(party_group %in% c("Republican", "Democrat")) %>%
  group_by(day_relative_to_election, party_group) %>%
  summarise(
    mean = diagis::weighted_mean(x = untrustworthy_flag_daily, w = weight),
    se = diagis::weighted_se(x = untrustworthy_flag_daily, w = weight),
    n = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    percentage = mean * 100,
    ci_lower = (mean - 1.96 * se) * 100,
    ci_upper = (mean + 1.96 * se) * 100,
    year = "2020"
  ) %>% 
  filter(day_relative_to_election <= 6)

# Combine both years for comparison
event_study_data_combined <- bind_rows(event_study_data_2020, event_study_data_2024) %>% 
  filter(day_relative_to_election <= 6)

print("Event study data summary:")
print("2024 Data:")
print(event_study_data_2024 %>%
      filter(abs(day_relative_to_election) <= 3) %>%
      select(day_relative_to_election, party_group, percentage, ci_lower, ci_upper))

print("2020 Data:")
print(event_study_data_2020 %>%
      filter(abs(day_relative_to_election) <= 3) %>%
      select(day_relative_to_election, party_group, percentage, ci_lower, ci_upper))
```
